Tackling the growing Neets crisis will be easier for the universities of Kent and Greenwich following their merger into the UK’s first "super-university", according to the group’s leadership.

Known as the London and South East University Group (LASE), the institution is now the third largest in the UK, accommodating more than 50,000 students across four campuses in London, Medway and Kent.

The chief executive said the merged institutions are "much stronger" together as the higher education sector faces ongoing financial strains.

University of Greenwich vice-chancellor and chief executive of LASE Professor Jane Harrington said the move enables the group to meet regional needs in ways they could not independently.

"If I was to look through south-east London going out we’ve got areas of urban deprivation, then you go out into Medway and Kent you’ve got areas of rural deprivation and then we’ve got areas of coastal deprivation," she said ahead of LASE’s official launch on Monday.

"It’s a real opportunity for us to address the very people that the government’s worried about.

open image in gallery Jane Harrington unveiling the 'LASE Gateway' ( PA )

"Everyone probably now is starting to be familiar with the term Neets – basically people who are not in employment, education, or training – and it’s those very young people that we can now actually really start to look at what skills do they need?

"How can we upskill them? How can we reskill them? How can we go out and actually attract them and work with our FE (further education) colleges so that they’ve got pathways that are accessible to them in ways we just couldn’t do on our own."

Between April and June, an estimated 981,000 young people aged 16 to 24 were classified as Neets. While down 30,000 on the previous quarter, the figure remains 30,000 higher than a year ago, according to the Office for National Statistics.

Prof Harrington said the merger has also reinforced the universities’ financial positions. It comes amid escalating financial pressures across the UK sector, with MPs on the Education Committee warning earlier this year of a "real risk" an English university could close due to insolvency for the first time.

The Office for Students, the higher education regulator in England, cautioned the committee that 24 providers risked insolvency and closure in the 12 months from last November, warning 45 per cent of higher education providers could face deficits for 2025/26.

Prof Harrington said: "International students are more difficult to bring into the UK; the cost of living’s gone up constantly; we’ve got more costs within the university; student fees after 12 years are now in a position where they can increase slightly but we don’t know what will happen after two years; and then we’re going to have an international levy imposed on us.

"So if you combine all of that, there isn’t a university in this country that doesn’t have to really look at their costs."

open image in gallery It is hoped that the merger will help tackle the Neets crisis in local areas ( PA )

Institutions are bracing for the international student levy, which will charge them £925 per student annually from 2028-29.

"We are much stronger now we’re together," Prof Harrington added.

"It doesn’t mean we’re immune to the changes; we’re not, but I do believe we’ll be able to get ourselves in a much stronger, firmer position more quickly."

LASE is drafting a lessons learned "blueprint" for the Department for Education to serve as a "model" group structure for other institutions. Prof Harrington admitted the undertaking was "not for the faint-hearted" but insisted it was worthwhile.

Following their legal merger last month, Kent and Greenwich universities will operate as distinct academic divisions under their current names, with students continuing to apply to and graduate from their chosen institution.

However, the unified structure allows the group to offer subjects previously unavailable to them individually, alongside shared access to campus libraries and wellbeing services.

In May, King’s College London and Cranfield University, based in Bedford, announced plans to merge in August 2027.

News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

News.title: Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions
News.content:
This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

News.title: Kimi Antonelli’s stunning home Italian GP victory all but seals first F1 title
News.content:
The 20-year-old also benefited from a perfectly-timed (from his perspective at least) mid-race virtual safety car when Lance Stroll retired his Aston Martin, which allowed Antonelli a cheap stop to switch to fresh mediums while Russell stayed out on used hards. But at some point you just have to take your hat off to the youngster.

Antonelli was irresistible. He had already surged from 19th on the grid to 12th by the time the red flag came out at the end of lap 2. He was up to sixth a couple of laps after the race resumed. And by lap 18 of a 53-lap race, he had passed Russell for the lead for the first time. That is some going.

Having caught up to Russell, the two Mercedes drivers engaged in an entertaining battle for a few laps, the pair of them yo-yoing in and out of the lead before Russell got past Antonelli on lap 23 and managed to make it stick.

But the key moment of the race came on lap 27 when Stroll stopped at the first chicane and the VSC came out. For Antonelli, the decision to switch to fresh mediums was clear. He was going to struggle to make it to the end of the race. Far better to drop a few positions and fight back on fresh rubber.

For Russell, it was far trickier. He was in the lead of the race. He was on hard tyres which he knew could get to the end of the race. And he also had the problem of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who at the time he was struggling to shake off.

Mercedes chose to keep Russell out there. In hindsight, it may have been the wrong decision. Had he stopped at that point, he would at least have stayed ahead of Antonelli, and on the same tyres. By staying out, he kept the lead but found himself relentlessly hunted down by the Italian.

By lap 49, the Italian had caught up to him. Antonelli botched his first attempt at reclaiming the lead, going wide onto the gravel at the first chicane. But he made no mistake one lap later as Russell was once again left licking his wounds.

News.title: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling
News.content:
“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

News.title: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw
News.content:
A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

News.title: Relentless Springboks give All Blacks 15 minutes of hell to lead series
News.content:
There will be no repeat of the All Blacks historic Test series victory in South Africa 30 years ago, after the home side ruthlessly ensured they will lead 2-1 going into the concluding weekend.

And the manner in which the Springboks blew away their fierce rivals in the last 15 minutes made Rassie Eramus’s men overwhelming favourites to finish the job in America next Saturday.

However, there were passages of this brutal battle that suggested that Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry could still produce a finale worthy of the billing if New Zealand can learn the lessons from this brutal encounter at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

There was a late Kiwi try to give the scoreboard a humdinger hue but Erasmus’s side were well deserving of their second victory in as many Saturdays over their fierce rivals, and credit to the South Africa coach for outwitting counterpart Dave Rennie without needing to change his starting XV just before the kick-off, like he did seven days before.

Amazing what one can do with a simple but chilling game plan. The old scoundrel knew that if he slowed it down and let his scrum walk round the All Blacks scrum that his backs would have the precious space.

Yet, however it might feel away from Springbok turf, New Zealand will still fancy their chances of levelling it, especially after matching their opponents’ haul of four tries. Their fly-half, Ruben Love, missed five simple-enough points and until that last quarter it was an even contest. Yet, as it tends to, South Africa’s physical intensity and their almighty scrum eventually prevailed.

News.title: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

News.title: ‘It’s just a useless gimmick’: Telegraph readers react to Dyson’s latest gadget
News.content:
Would you spend over £400 on a toothbrush? Telegraph readers aren’t convinced.

The new Dyson CameraJet has just launched, retailing for £419.99, which brushes, flosses and mouth-washes in one, with the help of a camera.

After Rebecca Astill gave her verdict on the gadget, we asked Telegraph readers for their views and whether Dyson can convince them to trade in their old faithfuls.

They share the toothbrushes they swear by, from manual to electric models, and whether they see any reason to upgrade. Here’s what they had to say.

Why readers are unconvinced

The majority of readers seem unconvinced by the CameraJet, with John arguing that a toothbrush and a smartphone “sounds like two accidents waiting to happen. Squirted in the eye with mouthwash as you drop the phone down the toilet”.

“It’s just a useless gimmick,” argues reader Donald Mckie, a retired NHS dentist. “The average patient wouldn’t have a clue what they would be looking at in their mouth on a phone screen,” he adds.

“Dyson as a brand is an aspiration for many but I don’t know how this appliance would improve anyone’s oral health.”

In his view, “the tank for the mouthwash at 12.5ml is far too small, the industry average will be somewhere near 250-300ml” to last long enough and successfully dislodge sticky plaque.

He also questions the picture quality of the camera with water spray, saliva, lips, facial hair and toothpaste in the way. “People nowadays will expect pin sharp detail, which I doubt this will deliver.”

Sports.title: ‘I had his head in my hands trying to keep him awake’ – Paul Ince recalls horror of Glenn Hoddle heart attack
Sports.content:
PAUL INCE has opened up about the “worst experience of my life” when he was desperately trying to keep Glenn Hoddle awake after his old England boss had suffered a heart attack.

The pair were doing punditry for BT Sport on October 27, 2018 – on Hoddle’s 61st birthday – when the Spurs icon had a cardiac arrest.



A quick-thinking sound engineer with first-aid training performed continuous CPR on Hoddle for eight to nine minutes, as well as using an on-site defibrillator to deliver a shock, before the paramedics arrived.

Ince consoled Hoddle by talking him through their shared football experiences as he held his former gaffer’s head in his hands – before the former Chelsea chief, thankfully, made a full recovery.



Ince said: “It was probably the worst experience in my life.

“We were playing table football and the next minute he just keeled over and had a heart attack, a cardiac arrest.



“I had his head in my hands trying to keep him awake, talking about the World Cup in ‘98, about our time at Wolves.

“I was probably sat there for about an hour until the medical people came. Now when I speak to him it’s on the golf course!”

It underlined to Ince the importance of everyone, ideally, being able to use a defibrillator.

Which is why the former Manchester United star, 58, is part of the campaign Every Minute Matters, where Sky Bet and the British Heart Foundation have a mission to put a stop to fear of using the life-saving equipment.



Research commissioned by Sky Bet and BHF claimed that 69 per cent of football fans surveyed believe fear could stop them using a defibrillator.

Ince added: “It shows you how important it is to get to people as quickly as possible when they’re in serious trouble.

“The fact that the defibs are in all these communities, if someone was to collapse now, 200 yards away you’d be able to get a defib machine.



“The machine does it for you, it’s not hard to work, so it’s a great, great cause.

“When I think about Glenn and see what he’s doing now, it brings a smile to my face.”

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon joins two Premier League legends in history books as England star lays on ANOTHER assist for Barcelona
Sports.content:
BARCELONA star Anthony Gordon made history in only his FOURTH match with his new club.

Gordon, 25, joined Barca in May following a £70million deal with Newcastle and signed a five-year contract at the Nou Camp.



And the winger has hit the ground running with the Blaugrana as he has already registered a staggering four assists in as many LaLiga appearances.

The ex-Everton star completed that amazing record in Barcelona‘s dominant 5-0 win at Valencia as he set up Fermin Lopez’s goal.



And the England international became only the third player to provide four assists in his first four matches in Spain’s top flight this century.

The other two are fellow ex-Premier League stars Cesc Fabregas and Luis Suarez.

What makes this record even more special is that all three players achieved it while playing for Barcelona.

Gordon‘s arrival ended the Blaugrana’s interest in signing Marcus Rashford on a permanent transfer last summer.

Rashford enjoyed a successful loan stint with the Catalan giants last season that saw him amassing a total of 14 goals and 15 assists in 49 appearances.

However, Barcelona opted against triggering the versatile forward’s £26m option to buy him from Manchester United.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Thus, Hansi Flick’s side decided to sign Gordon to fill in on the left wing and his recent record proved this was a wise choice.

But Rashford has been enjoying sparkling return to United’s squad after another move away never materialised during the summer transfer window.

The England international has played in all of Man Utd’s three Premier League matches this season.

And the forward has started in two of them as he gears up for a busy season in the Premier League and Champions league.

Sports.title: Three points from Chelsea’s defeat to Arsenal as missing stars dent Xabi Alonso’s title ambitions
Sports.content:
CHELSEA suffered their first defeat in the Premier League this season at the hands of London rivals Arsenal.

The Blues, who were missing some key players, became the first team to score against the reigning Premier League champions, who picked up a clean sheet in both of their first two games in the top flight.



And it was Morgan Rogers – the man the North Londoners identified as a priority summer signing before Chelsea hijacked the deal with a record £117million – who opened the scoring just two minutes after kick-off.

However, Arsenal hit back with former Chelsea star Kai Havertz on 25 minutes before captain Martin Odegaard completed the hosts’ comeback in the second half at the Emirates to seal their third win on the spin.



That led to Xabi Alonso‘s first Premier League defeat with his new club after winning his first two games in charge.

SunSport’s Dan King looks at three talking points following a match that left a lot to ponder on:



HOLD YOUR HANDS UP, EMI

Emi Martinez was signed because Chelsea wanted a goalkeeper who was less gaffe-prone and better with his feet than Robert Sanchez.

Not all five goals Martinez has conceded so far were his fault but the failure to stop Kai Havertz’s shot for the equaliser was very poor indeed.

Maybe the kick in the head he took early on in the game from Gabriel Magalhaes was a factor. But probably not.

The Argentine, booed on his latest return to the Emirates, made an important save from Gabriel before Riccardo Calafiori’s “goal” was rightly ruled out for offside.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Martinez denied Bukayo Saka in the first half and the save he made from the England man in the second kept his team in the game.

The 2022 World Cup winner will rightly complain about what is going on in front of him, with Chelsea and especially Maxence Lacroix looking shaky. But he has to hold his hands up when he makes a basic error like this.

CAICEDO AND COLWILL MISSED

Chelsea lost due to a goalkeeping howler and one very good goal. And they did not snatch a draw because of an excellent save.

But the absence of two of their best players from their spine proved crucial. Reece James and Romeo Lavia did pretty well in the first half to stand up to Declan Rice, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Odegaard.

But neither of them is capable of Moises Caicedo’s high-energy, high-commitment, 90-minute displays.



Without the Ecuadorian midfielder, Xabi Alonso’s side will always find it hard against top opponents.

The loss of defender Levi Colwill to injury for most of last season was a huge factor in the team’s struggles.

Despite being just 23, he brings composure and leadership to Chelsea. They also missed his defensive skills and ability to pass out from the back.

The Blues struggled to handle Kai Havertz’s movement and needed Colwill to help Wesley Fofana fight fires.



COLE PALMED OFF

Just when it seemed the real Cole Palmer was standing up again, he endured a frustrating time.

The control Arsenal had over the game was a factor, just as it was when he was anonymous for much of the win over Brighton.

In the first half, he struggled to make any impression, with just one tame shot and one cute pass which almost teed up Joao Pedro.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Palmer’s day was summed up when he burst through but could only fire a shot well off target — he was perhaps distracted by Morgan Rogers being cynically tripped by Declan Rice.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta’s staggering record against Chelsea revealed as Arsenal make Morgan Rogers eat his words
Sports.content:
WHEN Morgan Rogers picked Chelsea over Arsenal in July, he said he had joined “the biggest club in London”.

The £117million signing – and most expensive English player of all time – did have a say when the two sides clashed at the Emirates on Sunday.



Rogers opened the scoring with a volley after 77 seconds and stuck his tongue out at the Arsenal fans for good measure.

He showed he was up for the scrap by picking a fight with, of all people, his England team-mate Declan Rice.



But Arsenal got one over on their former transfer target by coming from behind to win 2-1.

That does not make the Gunners the biggest club in London.



That claim, and exactly how to judge it, is up for debate.

But what is crystal clear is that, with Mikel Arteta in charge of Arsenal, the head-to-head battle between these two capital heavyweights is completely one-sided.

Chelsea actually edged out Arsenal in Arteta’s second game in charge.

Since that festive fixture in 2019, though, it has been one-way traffic.

One Chelsea win in the next 17 meetings makes grim reading for the club, and for Rogers as he looks to back up his bold remark.

Chelsea have failed to beat the Gunners in any of their last TEN Premier League ties.

Take cup competitions into account and that grows to 12 without victory.



Overall, it is two Chelsea wins, four draws and 12 wins for the Gunners during Arteta’s tenure.

Sports.title: Ronald Koeman’s goalkeeper son scores TWICE including 101st-minute equaliser to rescue a point for his team
Sports.content:
RONALD KOEMAN’S son scored a stunning brace to rescue a point for his team – even though he is a GOALKEEPER.

Ronald Koeman Jr is the starting keeper for Dutch club Telstar in the Eredivisie.



Koeman Jr, 31, was between the sticks when his side hosted Cambuur at BUKO Stadion.

And Henk Brugge’s side played out a 2-2 draw that promises to be remembered for a very long time.



That is because both of the hosts’ goals were scored by the Dutch shot-stopper in an intense match that saw them playing with ten men for over 70 minutes following the dismissal of Nokkvi Peyr Porisson.

In fact, Koeman Jr proved to be the hero as he picked up Telstar when they were down by two goals.



And he did so by scoring two crucial penalties, which have proven to be his forte.

The Dutchman put his team up on the scoreboard on 63 minutes, shortly after Cambuur scored their second.

And Koeman Jr saved a point with a late pen in the 11th minute of stoppage time.

The goalie is following in his father’s footsteps albeit in a different position as Koeman Sr is known as one of the best sweepers in the history of the game.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

His dad reached legendary status with the likes of Ajax, PSV Eindhoven, Netherlands and Barcelona.

in fact, Koeman Jr was born in Spain back in 1995 when his dad played for Barca.

However, the keeper has spent his entire 14-year career playing in the Netherlands for the likes of Almere, TOP Oss and of course Telstar where he has been sine 2021 and counts a total of 164 appearances.

Koeman Jr is one of very few goalkeepers assigned as penalty takers in this day and age.

A number of legends made a name for themselves as the exception to the rule, such as Vincent Enyeama, Hans-Jorg Butt, Jose Luis Chilavert, Rene Higuita and Rogerio Ceni.

Sports.title: Liverpool hero Georginio Wijnaldum set to join new club on free transfer just days after being tipped for Chelsea move
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL hero Georginio Wijnaldum is reportedly set to join Saudi Arabian giants Al-Ittihad on a free transfer.

The former Reds midfielder, 35, is understood to have agreed a one-year deal with the option of a further 12 months.



Ben Jacobs claims Wijnaldum is already undergoing his medical ahead of completing the switch.

The Dutchman has been available for nothing after leaving fellow Saudi Pro League side Al-Ettifaq at the end of last season.



But his expected move to Al-Ittihad comes just days after he was tipped for a shock return to the Premier League with Chelsea.

Reports claimed the Blues had made contact over a possible short-term deal after Xabi Alonso was left short of options in midfield.

Chelsea sold Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for £125million before seeing a deadline-day move for Monaco ace Lamine Camara collapse.

That led to Wijnaldum emerging as a possible solution, with his huge amount of Premier League experience making him an attractive option.

The midfielder spent five years at Liverpool after joining from Newcastle in 2016, making 237 appearances and scoring 22 goals.

He became a key man under Jurgen Klopp and won the Premier League, Champions League, Club World Cup and Uefa Super Cup during a trophy-laden spell at Anfield.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Wijnaldum later joined Paris Saint-Germain before spending time on loan at Roma and then moving to Al-Ettifaq in 2023, where he enjoyed three seasons in Saudi Arabia.

And after scoring 17 times in 34 league appearances last term, Wijnaldum now looks set to remain in the Middle East with Al-Ittihad – ending any immediate hopes of a surprise Chelsea switch.

Sports.title: Three points from Man Utd’s draw at Everton with Michael Carrick putting himself in the firing line again
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have given their fans more food for thought with an eventful 2-2 draw at Everton.

The lead they took via Benjamin Sesko‘s 88th-minute header was wiped out deep into stoppage time by Ainsley Maitland-Niles‘ long-range stunner.



And that has left the Red Devils with just four points from their first three Premier League matches this term – all of which they went into as overwhelming favourites.

SunSport’s Samuel Luckhurst offers up his three talking points from Hill Dickinson Stadium…



TELL IT LIKE IT IS

Michael Carrick says United have not had a bad start, but he’s wrong.

When a United manager comes out with stuff like that, it is just going to wind up supporters.

Going forward, he needs to look after himself a little bit more and be a bit more critical of the team.

It’s just not going to chime with fans. He sounds a bit too compliant, like Ole Gunnar Solskjaer did during his tenure, and that didn’t really get him anywhere.



WATCH YOUR BACK

Defensively, United are in a state of disarray after conceding six goals in their first three games.

There is no defensive midfielder in that team at the moment because it took so long to sign Carlos Baleba, so there is no shield for the back-four.

But you look at the full-backs – Luke Shaw and Diogo Dalot first started together eight years ago – so there is possibly some backwards thinking there.

Harry Maguire looked a little bit leggy. He has never been the quickest, but at 33 he is only going to get slower.

Lisandro Martinez is not particularly quick either.



United look so open and gettable. Everton had twice as many attempts on target, so if they were a bit more clinical, maybe they’d have had an even better day.

LAM TO THE SLAUGHTER

Senne Lammens probably had his worst game for United.

He dropped a pretty straightforward cross in the first half, punched away a catchable effort, and was culpable for Tyrique George‘s goal.

Sports.title: Three points from Arsenal’s win over Chelsea as Arteta will be left feeling smug over questionable transfer policy
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA could hardly have asked for a better answer to the questions surrounding Arsenal’s summer transfer business.

The Premier League champions came from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 at the Emirates and make it three wins from three to start their title defence.



Morgan Rogers, one of Arsenal’s big summer targets before his £117million move to Chelsea, threatened to make them regret missing out when he fired the visitors ahead after just 77 seconds.

But Kai Havertz levelled midway through the first half before skipper Martin Odegaard completed the turnaround after the break.



And with several of Arteta’s big calls paying off, SunSport looks at three talking points from another statement win.

Havertz outclassed his former club in style

Arsenal’s decision to leave themselves looking light in attack after the transfer window raised plenty of eyebrows.

Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Leandro Trossard were all moved on, Ethan Nwaneri left on loan and Christos Tzolis was their only new wide attacking arrival.

But Havertz provided the perfect reminder of why Arteta was happy to stick with what he had.

The former Chelsea man dragged Arsenal level with his first-half strike before playing his part in the winner by allowing Tzolis’ delivery to run through for Odegaard.

Havertz may not always be the flashiest No9 in the Premier League but his movement, work-rate and intelligence remain hugely important to this Arsenal side.

And after Rogers had given Chelsea the lead, Arteta will have enjoyed seeing a player already in his building provide the response.

Konsa looks at home

Ezri Konsa was handed his first Arsenal start after arriving from Aston Villa in a deal worth around £51million last month.

The England defender came in for the injured Cristhian Mosquera and, despite Arsenal being rocked inside two minutes, soon settled alongside Gabriel.

Arteta has been criticised before for repeatedly spending big on defenders, but Konsa’s arrival already looks capable of giving him another reliable option across the back line.

With William Saliba sidelined long-term, Arsenal moved quickly for an experienced Premier League defender rather than gambling on their existing depth.



Against one of the league’s most dangerous attacks, that decision looked an increasingly sensible one.

Tzolis shows why Arsenal signed him

Tzolis arrived from Club Brugge for around £34m after producing 17 goals and 23 assists in their title-winning campaign last season.

And the Greece international showed another glimpse of why Arsenal were prepared to make him their main attacking addition.

His dangerous second-half ball eventually found Odegaard after Havertz’s clever dummy, allowing the captain to fire Arsenal ahead.



There were plenty who felt Arsenal should have added another superstar attacker before the window shut.

But Havertz scoring, Tzolis helping create the winner and Konsa impressing on his first start made this about as good an afternoon as Arteta could have hoped for.

Three points on the pitch and perhaps a few points proved off it too.

Sports.title: 'I'm back with a bang' - Littler topples Humphries to take glory in Prague
Sports.content:
Luke Littler beat rival Luke Humphries to win on his return to the European Tour at the Czech Darts Open in Prague.

Littler had not played in a European Tour event since March, but roared to glory with an 8-6 victory in Sunday night's final to end his opponent's hopes of winning this title for a third straight year.

Littler hit five 180s and averaged just over 95 as both players struggled in the heat at the PVA EXPO after a long day which had already seen The Nuke overcome Michael van Gerwen in the semi-finals, Danny Noppert in the quarter-finals and Krzysztof Ratajski in the last 16.

"It's good to be back and I'm back with a bang," said Littler after his victory.

World No 1 Littler won the first two legs against world No 2 Humphries in Sunday's final, only to see his rival, who has reached four of the last five finals in this tournament, reel off three straight legs to take the lead.

Littler fought back to move ahead with a 130 checkout in the ninth leg - the biggest finish of the game - and then won the next two legs to move 7-4 ahead in a race to eight.

Humphries rallied to win the next two legs and was millimetres away from sending the game to a decider, as he wired two darts at D16.

Littler recovered to pin D10 to win this tournament for the first time, taking home the £35,000 first prize and guaranteeing his place at the European Championship in Dortmund in October.

That's one of the titles that Littler wants to win as he eyes a clean sweep of major trophies in 2026 - and it means he's unlikely to play in any other regular European Tour events this season.

Image: Luke Littler celebrates at the Czech Darts Open (Pic: Sebastian Doppstadt/PDC Europe)

"I'm not sure now I've won this one," he explained. "I think I've secured my place in Dortmund. That's obviously the one I'm chasing.

"In two weeks time it's the World Series in Amsterdam. We'll have to see what happens, what the plan is and how busy I am."

Humphries had overcome Gerwyn Price, William O'Connor and Andrew Gilding earlier on Sunday to reach the final for the third year in a row, but he was not upset at missing out on a 'three-peat'.

"I can't be upset," he said. "The two darts I threw at D16 were right on the wire and if that goes in, it could have been a different game.

"That's just the way it goes. He's a fantastic player. I've been playing here and there, not so great. Maybe good sometimes. I've got to dedicate my life a bit more to get better and keep pushing him.

"I keep saying I'm not beating him in finals so I've got to change things to keep matching him.

"I think he enjoys the challenge and I love it as well. Hopefully over the next four months, I push him and if he does the clean sweep [of major titles] he has to do it the hard way."

Sports.title: Great Britain and Ireland claim historic win in Walker Cup thriller
Sports.content:
Great Britain and Ireland won the Walker Cup for the first time since 2015 after a nerve-shredding late comeback saw them beat the USA by a 13½-12½ scoreline.

Dean Robertson's side looked to be heading for defeat at Lahinch after suffering a clean sweep of defeats in the Sunday morning foursomes and with the Americans three points ahead going into the singles matches.

But the home side lost only two of the 10 matches and the competition eventually came down to the very last as Josh Hill won the 18th hole of his match with Tyler Watts to seal an incredible victory.

The USA will be left to regret the late turnaround after four missed putts to retain the Walker Cup.

Team GB&I needed a quick start to produce any sort of comeback and they delivered after Stuart Grehan, Luke Poulter - son of former Ryder Cup star Ian - Jack Whaley and Tyler Weaver all won their matches.

However, the Americans steadied the ship after securing halves through Miles Russell and Kihei Akina and wins courtesy of Ryder Cowan and Josiah Gilbert as it looked like they had thwarted the comeback.

As it looked like the Americans were about to take a firm grip on yet another win, Team GB&I responded once again. Eliot Baker overcame Stewart Hagestad on the final hole to ensure the Walker Cup would be determined on the final hole.

Hill and Tyler Watts were all square coming down the last at County Clare and Hill produced a stunning up-and-down from the bunker to complete a thrilling comeback and seal the unlikeliest of wins.

Image: Great Britain and Ireland celebrate after winning the Walker Cup for the first time since 2015

Speaking after securing the decisive point, Hill said: "This is absolutely unbelievable. It doesn't get better than this."

Captain Robertson added: "We are so elated. We're hardly able to put it into words. There's a lot of emotion, a lot of happy tears. But pride is the word I would use to describe this.

"There was most definitely a belief in the players and even though we were swept 4-0 this morning, there wasn't a despondency.

"The boys have delivered and I am incredibly proud of each and every one of them."

The victory by GB&I ends the streak of five victories in the Walker Cup by the USA and is their 10th win overall.

USA captain Nathan Smith refused to criticise his players, saying: "The match was incredible. It was definitely a tale of two days with what happened this morning and going forward now and how they played this afternoon.

"We knew how great their team was. They're a great team. They're a deep team. We knew they were capable of anything. Really at no time did we take the foot off the accelerator.

"All you can do is really tip your cap to them. They played great."

Sports.title: 'Just unheard of! - Antonelli's miracle win likened to 'walking on water'
Sports.content:
On a Monza weekend that had already produced one implausible result in qualifying, Italy's new young star Kimi Antonelli delivered a second in Sunday's thrilling race to ensure its own prominent place in Formula 1's history books.

Of course, unlike surprise pole position sitter Pierre Gasly - who had never previously qualified at the head of an F1 grid in 190 appearances spent in mostly midfield cars - the 20-year-old Antonelli has become a fixture at the head of the field this year.

Sunday represented the seventh race win of the Mercedes driver's increasingly-impressive second of Formula 1 and one which extended what stood as a 59-point championship lead to a joint season-high 66 points.

But by winning from the second-lowest grid position in F1's 76-year history - 19th place - and beating a team-mate and chief title rival in George Russell who had started from the front row, Antonelli ensured it was anything but just another win.

And that's before you even consider the local factor too - Antonelli ended a 60-year wait for an Italian to win their home Grand Prix again.

The remarkable Monza comeback led to Antonelli being described as "King Kimi" by Martin Brundle, who has both raced against and commentated on many of the sport's most legendary figures over more than four decades.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Italian Grand Prix.

Brundle's fellow Sky Sports F1 pundit Nico Rosberg, the 2016 world champion, was similarly effusive in his praise after witnessing Antonelli's remarkable drive.

"We have to say the race that he drove, the first lap, the second start, everything was to perfection," said Rosberg.

"The speed he had, how he was managing everything. You cannot do it better.

"He's in his second season in F1, he just turned 20. Who does that like that? It's just unheard of!"

'He's going to walk over water' - Wolff thought 'special moment' was possible

Rosberg had been among the many ahead of the race to suggest that a podium was likely out of Antonelli's reach from the grid's penultimate row, something the Italian himself had ruled out after qualifying.

But it turns out that not everyone was expecting it to necessarily be a race purely of damage limitation from the grid penalties that had left Antonelli so out of position.

"I thought one of the two [Mercedes drivers] is going to win," disclosed Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff after the race.

"Either George because he was on pole [for the restart] or Kimi because he's going to walk over water here in Monza. And I felt that yesterday also."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli and George Russell go wheel-to-wheel for the Italian Grand Prix lead in several epic team-mate battles.

Wolff, who worked with Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes for six of the Briton's seven world titles, said he sensed "a special moment" was potentially in the offing from Antonelli at his home track.

"Its been a while that I've seen drivers' energy levels, mindset or behavioural pattern and I knew that that was his mission today, to win the race," he said.

"I chatted with his father yesterday, the father also saw that coming.

"These are the moments where you can see how a weekend is panning out through the sessions, that a special moment could come.

"It's still a mechanical sport, so it can change quickly."

What made the difference for Antonelli?

Like any great comeback story, Antonelli's was not without some good fortune along the way.

Certainly, the second race start after the red flag for Charles Leclerc's big lap-two crash offered a second chance to make up multiple places more quickly than otherwise might have made the chance had the race not been stopped, even if it did compromise Mercedes' plans for running Antonelli on a long hard-tyre opening stint.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc CRASHES OUT the of the Italian GP

He was already running 12th by the time the red flag was thrown. He then picked up four more places on the restart lap. By lap 13 he was directly behind Russell in third and, once Gasly's early challenge faded, the Mercedes' went head-to-head from lap 16 in what soon turned into an almost lap-by-lap changing of the lead.

Eventually running second as the battle settled down slightly, a later well-timed Virtual Safety Car then allowed Antonelli to make a pit stop to switch on to fresher medium tyres, with Russell soon locked in to going to the end on more-worn hards, although Wolff said it was not clear at the time which strategy would win the race.

In any case, Wolff believes it was Antonelli's driving on track overtaking cars that made the difference.

"The differentiator today was the ability going through the traffic," added Wolff. "We've seen it with other great ones in the past. Lewis put it in some of the races and that's what he's shown today.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli wins the Italian Grand Prix from 19th on the grid

"There's just no stopping when a driver and a car are one, then there's nothing that can stop them."

As for Italy's rising star himself, Antonelli said he had woke up on Sunday morning feeling "very good mentally" and "that a very good result would have been a podium for me".

"But after the red flag I was already P12 and I had another start," he added.

"After another couple of laps I was already in the top five and I knew I could have a shot for the win. Of course it was very difficult to break away but we managed to pull it off and bring it home."

Sports.title: 'There are no rules here' - Hamilton criticises Ferrari after Leclerc clash
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has accused Ferrari of having "no rules" after a clash with his team-mate Charles Leclerc during the Italian Grand Prix.

Hamilton launched an aggressive move up the inside of his team-mate at the first corner, but was then forced off onto the gravel himself on the exit of the chicane as Leclerc held onto the inside line.

Hamilton dropped from his starting position of fourth to 10th, and was left playing catch-up for the rest of the race, as he eventually finished sixth.

Leclerc held onto third after the incident, which featured contact between the pair, but then crashed out of the race on the second lap, leaving Ferrari to suffer a dismal afternoon at their home race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Italian Grand Prix.

"I think it comes down to rules of engagement," said Hamilton, who joined Ferrari from Mercedes in 2025.

"When I was at Mercedes, we had written rules of engagement.

"We never really, really had it too bad. There was a moment between me and Nico [Rosberg] a couple of times, but more often not, it was good.

"Here, there are no rules. We need to address that."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc crashes out of the Italian GP

Too late or too early for team orders?

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli claimed a stunning victory from 19th at the grid to extend his advantage over Hamilton to 76 points, while the Ferrari driver also fell 10 points behind George Russell as the Brit completed a Mercedes one-two.

It had been a topic of discussion in the media before the race as to whether Ferrari should prioritise Hamilton over Leclerc given his advantage in the standings, which was extended to 36 points by Sunday's result.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton says the team are 'too late' to implement any sort of 'Ferrari priority'.

Asked by Sky Sports F1 after the race whether he should have priority over Leclerc, Hamilton replied: "We are too far past that already. It's too late for that now.

"I lost a lot of points today to those guys.

"We will do our best to keep pushing the rest of the season but they are out now, out ahead of us."

Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur insisted that it was too early in the season for the team to prioritise one of their drivers.

Vasseur justified his position by using the example of McLaren's experience last year, when Oscar Piastri led Lando Norris in the standings before being hauled in by both his team-mate and Max Verstappen by the end of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Karun Chandhok was at the SkyPad to look at who was at fault after Lewis Hamilton went down to 10th position after this contact with Charles Leclerc.

"For sure, the outcome of the first corners is not good for the team," Vasseur said.

"Now, to see if we have a team order or whatever, I think that the good comparison that I made was that last year, Piastri was leading McLaren at this stage of the season and if McLaren put everything on Piastri, Max Verstappen would have been champion.

"For sure, at one stage you have to take a decision but I think it was too early to take a decision before Monza. Now we have time to discuss with the guys."

Leclerc: We went too far

Leclerc admitted that he and Hamilton had gone "too far" in their early battle, but questioned who was "forcing" a narrative playing the team-mates off against each other.

The Monegasque referred to the previous race in Zandvoort when Hamilton had been left frustrated by being held up by Leclerc during the race when the pair were on different strategies.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc explains what caused the Ferrari driver to crash out in the early stages of the Italian Grand Prix.

"I don't really know who is forcing that narrative that we are one against the other," Leclerc said.

"I mean, honestly, Zandvoort, there was way too many talks already.

"Here, it's true though that we went too far. I think Lewis in Turn 1, then Turn 2, I tried to do the tightest corner possible, but that was just not enough - and doing it here is not good."

Should Ferrari have pitted Hamilton?

Hamilton was also once more left frustrated by his team's strategic decisions, with the 41-year-old questioning both the choice of tyre compound for him after the early red flag, and a later decision not to pit him under a virtual safety car.

"It's one of the harder ones to swallow today," he told Sky Sports F1. "I was definitely hoping for more.

"I gave it absolutely everything. We just didn't have the speed on the straights and we were mostly a sitting duck to the guys around me.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico Rosberg says it is 'not feasible' for Ferrari to favour Lewis Hamilton at this stage of the season.

"We will look internally and try and figure out what we could have done better. I felt we should have been on the hard tyre [on the restart] but we also would have had to overtake people, because we were further back than we were supposed to be.

"I thought they were going to stop us [under the VSC] but they didn't stop us, so I ran out of tyres."

Vasseur said that Ferrari's difficultly overtaking due to a lack of straight-line speed meant they would have struggled to make an extra stop work in the way that Antonelli and Verstappen, who finished third, were able to.

"We were 10 seconds behind Max before the VSC and we finished 10 seconds behind," Vasseur told Sky Sports F1.

"If you do this [pit], you have to overtake and overtaking is not our favourite topic. It would have been more difficult."

Sports.title: Unlucky or unfair? Did Mercedes strategy cost Russell Monza win?
Sports.content:
George Russell feels Mercedes were correct to split strategies despite losing out to Kimi Antonelli in a thrilling Italian Grand Prix.

Russell led Antonelli, who stormed through the field from 19th to be in the lead battle after just 13 laps, by one second when a race-changing Virtual Safety Car was called with 25 laps remaining.

Mercedes pitted Antonelli, but not Russell, for new medium tyres, which put the team-mates 15 seconds apart when the VSC ended.

From sixth, Antonelli overtook his rivals one by one then caught and overtook Russell with three laps to go to win his home event.

It leaves Russell 66 points behind Antonelli in the Drivers' Championship with 10 rounds to go.

"I was on the hard tyre and Kimi was on the medium tyre [when the VSC came], so if either of us were to pit, it was going to be Kimi," said Russell.

"I guess, why I was just a little bit annoyed with the timing of that VSC because, like Max said, I think it would have been tough for those guys on the medium to have competed with anybody on the hard tyre. But, it takes nothing away from Kimi's drive altogether."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The crowd erupted with boos aimed at George Russell as he stepped on Monza podium

Had Mercedes pitted both drivers, Antonelli would have been stuck behind for a few seconds in the pit lane, therefore losing track position to Max Verstappen, who also pitted under the VSC.

Russell told Sky Sports F1: "The VSC came at an awkward time. I don't think the team knew what the right strategy was and, as Max was in the fight, decided to split the strategy which was probably the right thing for the team to do.

"In hindsight of course, it's easy to say I should have pitted or, if I won the race, they would have said Kimi should have stayed out.

"I would have liked to have had a fight with Kimi. It was quite a nice battle and I felt I was holding my own at that point. That was probably another reason the team wanted us to go on a different strategy. I get it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli and George Russell go wheel-to-wheel for the Italian Grand Prix several times

Schiff: I don't know why Russell is not more frustrated Sky Sports F1's Naomi Schiff



"I don’t know why he’s not a little bit more frustrated, if I’m totally honest.



"I guess if you’ve given it all and you think that have actually executed the best strategy, and your team-mate has beaten you outright from P19 on the grid, then maybe there is nothing to be frustrated about, other than the fact that Kimi is going to be incredibly tough to beat this season."

Wolff explains Mercedes' thinking at time of VSC

Toto Wolff revealed Mercedes' computer systems told them, at the time of the VSC, that Russell's strategy would be faster than Antonelli's with the Italian expected to "come close but wouldn't catch".

Mercedes believed the hard tyre was a "forever tyre" that would effectively last the whole race, but not with the performance of the medium.

"The differentiator today was the ability going through the traffic [from Antonelli]. We've seen it with other great ones in the past. Lewis [Hamilton] put it in some of the races and that's what he's shown today," said Wolff.

"There's just no stopping when a driver and a car are one, then there's nothing that can stop them."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell explains why the team chose not to pit him during the VSC, which potentially could have cost him the win in Monza

Coming into the weekend, Antonelli was expected to lose points to his closest title rivals - Russell, Lewis Hamilton and Lando Norris.

Instead, he's extended his advantage and Russell is set to start at the back himself in one of the upcoming races as he does not have enough engines to finish the season without a grid penalty.

However, Russell says he's "not thinking about" the title race and instead is looking at the positives of being competitive in Monza and Zandvoort compared to the events before the summer break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli reflects on his sensational 19th to first Monza victory, catching teammate George Russell to claim a landmark home win and strengthen his championship lead

"We are where we are. Kimi's been driving incredibly this season and deserves to be leading the championship and he's got a healthy lead," he said.

"I'm not going to think about the fight or the comeback. I'm just thinking about going to every race and trying to win it. It will be what it will be. I'm not putting any pressure on myself in this regard, saying 'I need to do this or that'. I just need to win more races and, of course, he's in this spot."

Sports.title: ‘Exceptional performance’: Arteta hails fightback win and says best yet to come
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal are capable of hitting even greater heights after the Premier League champions sent a statement to their title rivals by fighting back from a goal down to beat Chelsea on Sunday.

Arteta’s side were under pressure after conceding for the first time this season when Morgan Rogers struck early at the Emirates Stadium, but the response to the setback was outstanding. Kai Havertz equalised before conjuring a brilliant dummy for a rejuvenated Martin Ødegaard to make it 2-1, ensuring that Arsenal moved level on points with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.

“It was an exceptional performance,” Arteta said. “I enjoyed every minute from beginning to end, and the beginning was tough. But the team responded in a spectacular way – the conviction, the determination, the quality. It was beautiful. It was a fascinating game.

“I think it’s an indication for us of how we are capable of ­performing at an even higher level than last ­season. It depends on how we maintain and sustain that desire, that humbleness, and continue every day to try to find a better version of myself and the team. We still have a lot to grow and a lot to offer. This is the ambition of the team.”

Arsenal and City are the only sides who have won their first three games, a statistic Arteta took as evidence that the league will be even harder this time. “It is going to be super hard, the margins you win games,” he said.

“We went to Villa Park a few days ago and it was really tough. Today again. We’ll go to Sunderland and it’ll again be so, so tough. We know every week is going to be like this but that’s what we prepare for.”

Arteta was delighted with an exceptional midfield display from Ødegaard. Arsenal’s captain looks fit after two years of injury problems and has started the campaign with three goals in four games.

“He feels, confidence-wise, I think one of the highest that I’ve seen him,” Arteta said of the Norwegian. “He has a point to prove from last season as well, missing so much football. Kai is the same. I don’t know how many times they played together in the last three years but probably not much. He is enjoying his football. He was running ­forward, having shots, creating for his teammates.”

Arteta, who hopes Cristhian ­Mosquera will make a swift recovery from a muscle problem, was similarly positive about Havertz after the ­German impressed against his old club. “He looks settled, he looks happy, in his personal life some great things have happened,” he said. “He looks fit, he looks happy and he is scoring goals.”

View image in fullscreen Kai Havertz (right) celebrates scoring Arsenal’s first goal with Christos Tzolis and Gabriel. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters

While Arsenal celebrated, ­Chelsea reflected on coming up short. The Blues were exciting in attack but defensive shortcomings led to their first defeat under Xabi Alonso, whose new team have conceded seven in their first three league games.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“My priority is to win games and it’s easier when you don’t concede many,” Alonso said. “This is something that we need to address. We want to be tighter, to be more clinical, more balanced. But this takes time.

“We wanted to compete, we came to win. We were not that far, but it went their way. We could have scored to make it 2-1 and you never know what happens. But the result is the result, I’m not fighting against that. It hurts. But this is the first defeat, it is going to be a long journey and it doesn’t have a big impact in our mood.”

Chelsea are without a clean sheet in their past 19 league games but Alonso did not want to park the bus. “I want to compete in the best possible way to win,” he said. “Today we didn’t want to sit deep from the first minute and to wait and to make a long game. We wanted to be active, we wanted to be protagonists in the pressing, sometimes to go higher, sometimes lower, to have good possessions. And we have done many right things. We need to make it better.”

Alonso was optimistic that Moisés Caicedo is not enduring a long-term issue after the midfielder missed out with injury. Caicedo is yet to start this season and it is uncertain if he will be back for Chelsea’s Carabao Cup tie against Leeds on Wednesday.

“It’s about assessing the risk,” Alonso said. “Probably last week we took him on too early and I don’t want to make the same mistake again.”

Sports.title: ‘No excuses’: Moyes says transfer troubles will not hurt Everton after United draw
Sports.content:
David Moyes praised Everton’s resilient response to a troubled week after his side twice came from behind to salvage a point against Manchester United through Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s long-range strike.

The deadline-day signing, who was introduced in the 77th minute after James Garner pulled up with cramp, preserved Everton’s unbeaten start to the season with a 25-yard effort in the 96th minute.

Tyrique George also scored a superb equaliser to lift the mood at Hill Dickinson Stadium after transfer deadline day had left Moyes with a weaker squad and only one striker in Thierno Barry.

The Everton manager insisted it had been easy to keep the negativity away from his players. “It was the exact opposite,” he said of the potential negative impact on his squad.

“I said to the players there would be no excuses from any of us and the players all agreed. The players hugely bought into it. It can hurt you being a player down but it can also have the opposite reaction.

“Sometimes when you have less players it means everybody has to be ready and you have to find a way of making it work. Who knows how it will go? It will be difficult when we have three games a week.”

Moyes also paid tribute to the quality of the goals from Maitland-Niles and George, who cancelled out finishes from Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko respectively.
