World.title: Gilas Pilipinas suffers back-to-back blowouts to Korea ahead of Asian Games
World.content:
DRIVE. Gilas Pilipinas' Sedrick Barefield and South Korea's Lee Hyun-jung during their tune-up game in Suwon, South Korea, on September 6, 2026.

Gilas Pilipinas fails to win either of its two tuneup games against South Korea — losses that underscore the daunting task of defending its Asian Games throne

MANILA, Philippines – Another slow start doomed Gilas Pilipinas as it absorbed a second straight loss to host South Korea, 69-42, to close out the Hana Bank Invitational in Suwon on Sunday, September 6.

The Nationals managed just four points in the opening quarter and never came within striking distance the rest of the way, failing to win either of their two tuneup games against the Koreans just days before opening their Asian Games campaign in Nagoya, Japan.

Sedrick Barefield put the Philippines on the board first with a midrange jumper before Korea unleashed a 19-0 run that set the tone for the blowout, mirroring its 81-55 rout of the same opponents two days earlier.

Led by Yu Ki-sang and Yeo Jun-seok, Korea enjoyed a lead as big as 37 points midway through the third quarter, 53-16, as it coasted to the breezy triumph.

Yu fired a game-high 15 points on a 5-of-8 clip from three-point land, Yeo finished with 14 points and 5 rebounds, while Lee Hyun-jung turned in an all-around outing of 11 points, 15 rebounds, 6 assists, and 2 steals.

Zavier Lucero paced the Philippines with 14 points, 6 rebounds, and 3 assists, but lacked sufficient help as no other Filipino player scored in double figures.

Adrian Nocum finished with 9 points and 3 assists, while Sedrick Barefield and Brandon Ganuelas-Rosser chipped in 7 points apiece in a defeat that underscored the Filipinos’ daunting task of defending their Asian Games crown.

With only 11 players in the lineup, Gilas Pilipinas has its fingers crossed that Justin Brownlee, the hero of the 2023 championship squad, will make it to the quadrennial showpiece.

From Korea, the Nationals will fly to Japan for the Asian Games, where the men’s basketball tournament runs from September 10 to 20.

Bunched in Group C, the Philippines will open the Asian Games against Bahrain on September 11, then tangle with Kazakhstan and China on September 12 and 14, respectively. – Rappler.com

World.title: 11-year-old Filipino hooper turns heads in Korea
World.content:
OVERSEAS STINT. Kael Mabulac during his stint for the Busan KCC Aegis in the Korean Basketball League Youth.

Kael Mabulac, the son of former PBA player Michael Mabulac, continues to carve out a name for himself after an impressive run in the Korean Basketball League Youth, where he represents KCC Busan Egis

MANILA, Philippines – It has only been two years since Kael Mabulac began taking basketball seriously, yet his budding career has already taken him overseas.

The 11-year-old son of former PBA player Michael Mabulac continues to carve out a name for himself, turning heads with an impressive performance in the Korean Basketball League (KBL) Youth.

In July, Kael was one of only five Junior Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League (MPBL) players selected to represent Busan KCC Egis in the KBL Youth, alongside Josh Cruz, Kenan Picazo, Jaiden Dimalanta, and Cholo Evangelista across different age categories.

Kael showed why he deserved the spot, leading the under-11 division in points (12.8), rebounds (9.4), and blocks (1.6) while ranking second in steals (2.6).

Kael steered the under-11 team of KCC, one of the most storied KBL franchises with a record-tying seven championships, to an unbeaten 4-0 run in the preliminary stage before it fell narrowly to eventual champions Seoul SK Knights in the semifinals.

“I was surprised and I was really happy because it’s a once-in-a-lifetime experience to play internationally even though I’m still young,” Kael told Rappler in Filipino.

Natural talent

Although Kael grew up around basketball, his father Michael — a Jose Rizal University standout who won three PBA championships with San Miguel and now plays for Biñan Tatak Gel in the MPBL — did not expect him to pursue the sport at such a young age.

In fact, Kael only started playing basketball in 2024, when a club competing in the City Hoops Basketball League needed a 2015-born player to complete its roster.

Michael said he was initially hesitant to let his son play, particularly because Kael had yet to receive any formal training.

“I was worried that he might embarrass himself because he had no training,” said Michael. “He might do all sorts of things — did he even know the rules of basketball? I was even thinking that he might end up shooting at the opposing team’s basket.”

But Kael held his own, and before long, he began outperforming his more experienced teammates.

“At first, I just watched daddy, and then I saw that playing seemed exciting and fun. I liked it too and it became something I did every day,” said Kael.

Seeing potential in his son, Michael eventually decided to put Kael through formal training — a decision that paid off as the younger Mabulac drew interest from several schools, including La Salle Green Hills, Xavier, Angelicum, La Salle Zobel, Mapua, and NU.

It also helps that Kael has a professional basketball player as a father, with Michael providing valuable advice that allows him to shake off bad habits and develop a more disciplined approach to the game.

“After every practice, I correct him. I tell him, ‘This is what you’re doing right and this is what you’re doing wrong.’ I think that’s one of his advantages, that his learning does not end in practice,” said Mabulac.

Young achiever

It did not take long for Kael to stand out, regularly posting triple-doubles and double-doubles across various leagues. One of his most notable performances came in the under-11 final of the Batang PBA, where he scored 45 points to lead Magnolia to the title.

Kael also earned back-to-back Most Valuable Player honors in his age division in the Junior MPBL Pocket League.

But it is not only in sports where Kael thrives.

According to his mother, Mori, Kael is also a consistent honor student at Lourdes School Quezon City, having finished fifth grade with high honors.

“He also qualifies for an academic scholarship. He’s already a scholar as a varsity player, but he also qualifies as an academic scholar. That makes me even more proud because he’s able to do both,” said Mori.

For Michael and Mori, it is important to let Kael enjoy being a child rather than push him too hard, allowing him to have fun, explore his interests, and develop at his own pace while balancing basketball and academics.

“When he doesn’t want to play or practice, I let him. He’s still a kid,” said Michael.

Big dreams

Like his idol, Gilas Pilipinas and Goyang Sono Skygunners star Kevin Quiambao, Kael dreams of playing professional basketball in the KBL. He also wants to compete in the Olympics and FIBA competitions.

Standing at 5-foot-6 and already possessing an all-around game, Kael appears to be on the right track, with KCC showing interest in him after a bone age assessment indicated promising growth potential.

According to Michael, Kael underwent the assessment in Korea and is projected to reach a height of up to 6-foot-7.

“I’m always asked what I want to be when I grow up. I always say that I want to play basketball. They ask me if there’s anything else I want to do, but I tell them, that’s really the only thing I want,” said Kael.

Michael, who knows the basketball scene all too well after spending more than a decade as a pro, believes that Kael can go as far as his perseverance will take him.

“I’m here to simply to guide him. I tell him, ‘You’re already lucky — you have the height and you already have scholarship opportunities.’ Hard work is the only thing he needs to add,” said Michael.

As Kael continues to climb the ranks and attract more attention, Mori hopes he remains grounded, reminding him that his career and talent can be taken away in an instant if he gets too full of himself.

Kael vows not to let that happen.

“I’ll always listen to them and follow their advice so I can continue to improve in both academics and sports and achieve my dreams when I grow up,” Kael said. – Rappler.com

World.title: Prosecution: ‘Impossible’ to call Fajarda as witness for now
World.content:
File photo of Vice President Sara Duterte and former Department of Education (DepEd) special disbursing officer Edward Fajarda during House panel hearing.INQUIRER PHOTO/LYN RILLON

MANILA, Philippines – Former Department of Education (DepEd) special disbursing officer (SDO) Edward Fajarda is unlikely to be called as witness in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial after he was advised to rest for another 30 days, House prosecutor Rep. Joel Chua said on Monday.

Fajarda was SDO during Duterte’s tenure as education secretary when P112.5 million in confidential funds were disbursed from the first to third quarters of 2023.

Prior to standing as witness for the prosecution, Fajarda suffered a stroke.

Article continues after this 

“Unfortunately, kahapon kasi nakita ko sa Viber group namin, yung medical bulletin na inissue kay Edward Fajarda kung saan inaadvise siya na another 30 days na pagpapahinga. With that, imposible na masalang namin siya today,” Chua told the media in an interview.

(Unfortunately, yesterday I saw in our Viber group, the medical bulletin issued to Edward Fajarda advising him of another 30 days of rest. With that, it is impossible for us to see him today.)

READ: Duterte trial: Ex-DepEd SDO Fajarda’s appearance moved to Sept. 7

As a remedy, the prosecution hopes to pursue stipulations that Fajarda may have likewise stated if he took the witness stand.

“Hindi naman natin pupwedeng ipilit yung tao, baka habang nakaupo sa witness stand baka may mangyari pa diyan… For humanitarian reason naman, mas gugustohin natin na stipulation na lang. Tutal yung sasabihin niya naman narinig na natin sa committee on good government,” Chua added.

Article continues after this 

(We can’t force the person, maybe while sitting on the witness stand something might happen… For humanitarian reasons, we would prefer to just stipulate. After all, we already heard what he said in the committee on good government.)

In 2024, Fajarda revealed at the House committee on good government and public accountability that he handed DepEd’s secret funds to Duterte’s security officer, Col. Dennis Nolasco.

Article continues after this 

The Commission on Audit previously flagged the transfer as only the SDO and head of agency may disburse the secret funds. /jpv

World.title: Antipolo Diocese to build retirement home for elderly, retired priests
World.content:
INQUIRER FILES

LUCENA CITY — Elderly and retired priests of the Diocese of Antipolo will soon have a home where they can receive care after decades of serving their communities.

Antipolo Bishop Ruperto Cruz Santos invited the faithful to witness the groundbreaking ceremony on Sept. 12 for the “Residencia Sacerdotal Obispado de Antipolo,” a retirement home for priests “who have devoted their lives to serving the Church and their communities.”

READ: Retirement should be what you want it to be – InLife

Article continues after this 

“For decades, our priests have stood beside us in every season of life. They baptized our children, blessed our homes, comforted us in sickness, guided us in confusion, and prayed for us in silence,” Santos said in an invitational message posted on the diocese’s official Facebook page.

The bishop did not provide details of how the planned Residencia Sacerdotal would look like, saying instead that it would be “a home of rest, dignity, and fraternity,” where elderly and retired priests would continue their ministry at a gentler pace.

“It is our promise that no priest will grow old alone, and no priest will be forgotten,” Santos said.

The Diocese of Antipolo has 78 parishes, including three quasi-parishes, and covers the entire province of Rizal and Marikina City. /jpv

World.title: 1 dead, 8 rescued as motorboat capsizes off Liwagao Island
World.content:
Occidental Mindoro. INQUIRER FILES

CALAPAN CITY — Eight passengers were rescued while one was reported dead after a motorboat bound for Occidental Mindoro capsized in waters off Liwagao Island in the Antique town of Caluya, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said Sunday.

Coast Guard Sub-Station (CGSS) San Jose, launched a search and rescue operation after motorboat SAN AGUSTIN IV failed to arrive at Barangay Caminawit in San Jose town, Occidental Mindoro.

READ: Occidental Mindoro under state of calamity, over P2.1 billion damage

Article continues after this 

The vessel departed Semirara Port in Antique on Sept. 5. Its owner later alerted the PCG after losing communication with the crew.

Despite difficult weather and sea conditions, rescuers located SAN AGUSTIN IV capsized off Barangay Sibulo in Liwagao Island, at around 6:30 a.m. on Sept. 6.

The eight survivors were found clinging to the boat’s keel and were immediately rescued by the PCG.

They were brought to Pinagpala Port in Barangay Semirara for medical evaluation and further assistance, in coordination with CGSS Semirara and the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office.

The PCG reported a fatality but did not immediately release details.

CGSS Semirara personnel aboard the MTUG Jun Yeu began towing the capsized motorboat toward Semirara Island. /dp

World.title: 11 Aeta communities get food aid as swollen rivers cut off access
World.content:
Volunteers load food supplies onto a Philippine Air Force helicopter for delivery to remote Aeta communities in Botolan, Zambales, on Sunday, Sept. 6. Photo courtesy of Zambales PDRRMO

SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — For more than seven hours on Sunday (Sept. 6), rescuers and local officials worked to deliver food to 11 Aeta communities cut off from the rest of Botolan town as swollen rivers and impassable roads prevented regular access to their remote villages.

The prolonged relief operation involved the Philippine Air Force airlifting food supplies to nine communities, while provisions for two others were hauled using carabao-drawn carts, according to Rolex Estella, head of the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office.

READ: Zambales floods displace over 6,000 residents

Article continues after this 

The operation was carried out as continuous rains caused strong currents in the Bucao River and two tributaries draining from Mount Pinatubo, isolating the communities in the eastern part of Botolan, locally known as Baytan.

The danger posed by the swollen waterways was underscored earlier in the week when a carabao-drawn cart carrying a father and his 5-year-old daughter was swept away by a strong current while they were traveling home to Barangay Palis.

Both were later found dead, highlighting the risks faced by residents who rely on river crossings to travel between the remote communities and the town proper.

READ: Zambales under state of calamity after widespread flooding, damage

Gov. Hermogenes Ebdane Jr. on Friday (Sept. 4) ordered the PDRRMO and municipal disaster management officials to closely watch lahar channels in the province after a forecast of more heavy rainfall from the southwest monsoon.

Article continues after this 

Estella said they established separate landing sites in the villages of Villar, Poonbato, and Cabatuan, so that residents from neighboring barangays could also receive the airlifted supplies.

A total of 4,564 family food packs were distributed 2,519 affected families from Villar, Moraza, Belbel, Burgos, Nacolcol, Palis, Maguisguis, Cabatuan, Owaog Nebloc, Malomboy and Poonbato, located about 25 to 30 kilometers from the Botolan town proper.

Article continues after this 

According to Ebdane the relief operation conducted jointly by the provincial government and the Botolan local government unit (LGU) was in response to the immediate needs of Aeta communities that mostly relied on farming for livelihood, but couldn’t bring products to lowland markets due to inclement weather.

Zambales was placed under a state of calamity on Aug. 19 after the combined effects of the southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones caused more than P591.98 million in damage to agriculture and infrastructure in the province. /jpv

World.title: 2 Pampanga engineers sacked over safety lapses after man’s death
World.content:
INQUIRER FILES

MANILA, Philippines — Two engineers from the Pampanga 3rd District Engineering Office of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) have been relieved of their duties for failing to comply with safety measures following a man’s death after he fell into an open drainage canal.

In a memorandum shared by the DPWH with the media late Sunday, Secretary Vince Dizon ordered the relief of Aser Mallari, officer-in-charge of the Office of the District Engineer, and Agustin Dagsaan Jr., officer-in-charge of the Office of the Assistant District Engineer, citing their “failure to comply with the required safety standards.”

READ: Man dies after falling into open drainage canal in Angeles City

Article continues after this 

The order is effective immediately.

The engineers are instructed to conduct inventory, accomplish, complete, and sign pending documents to ensure smooth turnover of their responsibilities in their respective offices.

Last August 28, Reiner Novero died after falling into a flooded, open drainage canal along the Fil-Am Friendship Highway in Barangay Cutcut in Angeles City, Pampanga. As seen in closed-circuit television footage circulating in social media, Novero was swept away by the strong current when he fell into the canal.

READ: Netizens bash Angeles City mayor over late suspension of classes

After an hour, Novero was recovered two kilometers from where he fell and was found beneath a bridge in front of a subdivision in Barangay Sto. Domingo.

The incident sparked safety concerns among many social media users pointing out why a drainage canal was left open. /jpv

World.title: Duterte trial Day 22: PSA official to testify on CF payees’ identities
World.content:
The Senate Impeachment Court. INQUIRER PHOTO / NIÑO JESUS ORBETA

MANILA, Philippines — As Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial opens its 10th week on Monday, the prosecution panel intends to verify the identities of the recipients of Duterte’s confidential funds (CFs).

Scheduled to testify on the 22nd trial date is Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) Assistant National Statistician Marissa Grande.

In the past weeks, the House prosecution presented the acknowledgment receipts submitted by the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) as proof of CF disbursements from late 2022 until the third quarter of 2023.

Article continues after this 

READ: 5 witnesses left in VP secret funds scrutiny – prosec

The receipts both offices submitted to the Commission on Audit raised eyebrows when seemingly suspicious names — resembling food, phrases, brands and animals — were listed as payees.

These names include Mary Grace Piattos, Miggy Mango, Nova Santos, Andy Lim, Antonio Pagong, Xuniso Belat and Shane Ngitngit.

Several names listed as recipients were first unveiled when the House Committee on Good Governance and Public Accountability launched an inquiry into Duterte’s secret funds in 2024.

Following the hearings, the PSA reported that 1,322 payees from the P500-million OVP CFs had no birth records.

World.title: Water, forest and neighborhood to decide future of Baguio constructions
World.content:
Despite thick fog, residents and guests boarded newly built rental boats when Burnham Lake reopened on Sept. 1, 2026, during Baguio City’s 117th charter day celebrations. The lake had been closed for renovations since 2025. Photo by Vincent Cabreza

BAGUIO CITY – The latest Baguio land use plan may correct decades of unregulated overdevelopment in the summer capital that has been blamed for its woes over dwindling water supply, overpopulation, diminished tree line and horrendous traffic jams that began as far back as the 1980s.

Water, the environment, the natural risks and fragilities of Baguio such as sinkholes, and the impact on the livability of surrounding communities will now dictate what future building investments shall be allowed to proceed under the latest city land use plan (CLUP) and proposed reforms to the zoning ordinance now being discussed by the Baguio City Council.

READ: Baguio water sources see rising turbidity due to incessant rains

Article continues after this 

If new building investments are not supported by sufficient water supply at their preferred locations or if the size and network of access roads to future structures are inadequate, these business endeavors may not get the blessings of the local zoning board and City Hall under the new CLUP, said architect Donna Tabangin, city planning, development and sustainability officer during a special session on Friday (September 4) of the Baguio City Council.

Overdevelopment had been one of the key concerns of Baguio’s redevelopment. At one point, Mayor Benjamin Magalong had contemplated imposing a moratorium on building constructions in 2019.

Tabangin said policy reforms being contemplated by the new CLUP are guided by the 2019 urban carrying capacity study which concluded that many Baguio resources are no longer sufficient for the modern population. For example, the city breached the carrying capacity of its water supply (0.15 square meters per person per day) in 2002, but the water utility has been rationing tap water much earlier to stretch supplies until rains come to replenish its aquifer.

“So future development projects must be driven by the carrying capacity of their areas. If water supply is insufficient, we cannot allow high density development there,” Tabangin told the Council.

But Baguio, a highly urbanized city that serves as a top tourist destination and a north Luzon education center, will not be turning away investments either, she emphasized.

Article continues after this 

Private and public developers, who incorporate solutions for areas with resource restrictions, can push through because investments would also be “incentives-based,” Tabangin said.

“As long as the carrying capacity allows it and the community benefits,” good builders and developers would be rewarded with additional floor space or an extra building floor when their projects guarantee services to the public, according to the CLUP presentation.

Article continues after this 

More importantly, new investments, from both public and private endeavors, would now follow “risk-informed planning,” guided by geophysical risks analyzed and mapped out by scholars and government experts.

According to Tabangin, geotechnical studies have determined that Baguio is more vulnerable to landslides (39 percent) rather than earthquakes (28 percent), floods (11 percent), sinkholes (17 percent), and forest fires (5 percent). Businesses used to believe that the summer capital was more prone to seismic risks, partly due to Baguio’s destruction when it was rocked by the 1990 Luzon earthquake, she said.

The city’s vulnerability map has become essential because of Baguio’s limited space, and investors have started penetrating inner city neighborhoods.

It says 53 of Baguio’s 128 barangays with a combined span of 434 hectares are classified as “very low” risk in a multiple hazard chart, while 34 villages with a combined 844-hectare coverage are “low” risks. The map says 28 villages covering 1,997 hectares are “moderate” risks, but 11 barangays spanning 2,423 hectares are “high” risks and 2 with a combined 52 hectares are labeled “very high.”

The city will require public investments to build over a thousand grade school and high school classrooms to address a backlog and hire more than 2,000 teachers, Tabangin said. It also needs to build housing for 28,123 informal settlers, of whom 3,032 reside in danger zones, she added.

Even government projects must heed the policy reforms, Tabangin said, because of recent findings that some roads turned out to have triggered slope erosions.
